text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Fitness 140 Upright Exercise Bike (Discontinued) I started my hunt for an exercise bike by driving around town and trying exercise bikes in stores. What I learned from this exercise is that not all exercise bikes are equal, and that a lot of them have an uncomfortable geometry with regard to where the seat and handlebars are located. For this reason, I would not recommend buying a bike that you have not tried in a store, because what you get may not fit you correctly. I chose the Schwinn 140 because when I tried it in a store I was happy with its comfort and performance.

Overall, I am extremely pleased with this purchase. This said, I have some other remarks. With regard to the assembly, I took my time, followed the directions, and it ended up taking most of an afternoon to assemble. The screws and knobs were vacuum sealed to a piece of cardboard, so I do not see how any of the parts could be missing or damaged. One tip I have for would-be assemblers is to record the serial number before assembly. On this model, the serial number turned out to be on the bottom of one of the supports, and the bike would have to be turned over to get to it once assembled. Once I had it together, I found that a couple of parts were loose and I had to go in and tighten them the next day. However, once I hopped on to give it a try, I found that it wasn't working. There was no resistance when I peddled.

I called customer support, and found that Schwinn was a division of Nautilus. Nevertheless, I was soon connected with the correct support person, and she was very efficient at diagnosing the problem over the phone. She told me I needed a new motor and that it would be shipped from Oregon and arrive in a week. Also, she called a repair man who contacted me the next day about the repair. For this reason, I am glad that I selected a Schwinn as opposed to another brand because I doubt that I could've gotten better or even equal customer support anywhere else.

A week later, the repair man arrived to install the part. He was EXTREMELY competent, and he tore the machine completely apart and rebuilt it. He diagnosed the problem as being in the cable as opposed to the motor, and he was able to replace the cable from parts in his truck. At this point, I feel completely confident that the machine is in 100% working condition and will not fail, due to the competency of the rebuilder.

Once I was able to start using the exercise bike, I started encountering problems with the seat. The seat is quite large, and on first sitting it is quite comfortable as well. However, as the days went by, I found that my buttocks were rubbing together and creating a sore in the vicinity of my coccyx. I gave it a lot of thought and concluded that the seat was too big for me. I went to the store and purchased a ladies size bicycle seat to replace it with, and so far I am more comfortable. I would advise anyone buying this machine to not replace the seat right off. It is not a bad seat, and you should use it for a while to see how compatible it is with your own seat. If you find it uncomfortable, you may, like me, choose to replace it with an ordinary bicycle seat rather than an exercise bicycle seat. My personal feeling about gel padding is that it is unnecessary, though it is built to some extent into regular bicycle seats. However, after using your bike for a while, you may decide to go with the padding after all. The point I'm trying to make is that if you have trouble with the seat it may be because it was designed to look good on an exercise bike more than to function as a bicycle seat, and if you have trouble with it it might be because it is just too big and flat.

I like very much using this exercise bicycle. It is solid, smooth, and quiet, with gentle transitions between the resistance levels. I am able to track my heart rate by holding the handlebars in the metal zone. The computer took a bit of getting used to, and actually technical support at Schwinn helped me get it set up to begin with. They are very nice, and actually American, which was a pleasant change for technical support. There are a number of pre-programmed exercise programs, and you are also able to create your own if you feel like it. I have not gotten to the point where I feel like creating my own, so I use the pre-programmed exercises.

I would recommend this exercise bicycle to anyone contemplating this purchase. From reading other peoples reviews, it does seem that having an exercise bike shipped to you bears the risk of not arriving in working condition, but Schwinn is very good at making it right for you so that you don't have to figure out how to get it back in the box and ship it back. I did check exercise bicycles around town, and the local stores wanted to charge a high price for delivering the bike and an even higher price for setting it up for you, so buying it from Amazon is an attractive alternative.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Fitness 140 Upright Exercise Bike (Discontinued)

text_fidelity_a: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills There is one huge flaw in this machine...and that is if you intend to use the incline feature you will no longer be able to reach anything out in front of you, meaning you can not reach your water bottle...music device...digital read out display...or even to use the heart rate grip handles.  If you look at the machine in the pictures...you will notice a black plastic insert that runs on top of the actual tread mill just below the display.  As you incline the machine...this part of the treadmill comes closer to you....meaning you have to move more backwards on the machine in order to avoid stepping on it.  You have to move back so far that you literally have to bend over at the waist just to use the heart rate grips.  I found myself keep having to step on the sides off the treadmill and stop my walk anytime I wanted to change my music or change a feature on the unit.  Very very frustrating. If you walk for say 30 to 60 minutes and you watch videos on youtube or something like that...you will have to literally stop walking and step off the machine as many times as the videos run out...or your music choice changes.  I don't hold onto the rail in front of me anyway, but if you are someone who does...you will not be able to do so with the unit inclined.  You will keep stepping on the plastic piece and can literally injure yourself the first time you do it.  Machine seems nice otherwise but this is to huge of a flaw to give it anything but 1 star.  I guess everyone else is not using the incline feature.  And no...I am not 8 feet tall....with long legs. Only 5'10" and my wife is 5'1" and has the same issue. My husband put it together in a couple of hours. The only time he needed my help was to assemble the parts that goes under the machine that makes it able to fold.
Once ready it is pretty sturdy. Obviously not as the ones at the gym, but mostly because it is smaller. The “bed” is shorter than the pro, but that’s exactly why it is perfect for a house, in my case for my garage. It is somewhat light weight. You can move it a little.
As soon as you press start it ask you to connect it with IFIT. I did not do that. I pressed the iFit button for 30 seconds and it was override. You CAN use it without the app. BUT, I bought the 5’’ screen. I can’t watch anything more than my stats there. Maybe if you buy the machines with larger screens the iFit app could be a good idea. The machine is very smooth. No weird sound beside the normal sound of the belt running.
This machine does not have a fan (I don’t need it) , and has good speakers.
I do mostly sprints, so I move from power walking with encline for 1 minute to all out for 1 minute for 15-20 min, and the machine works perfectly in those speeds and incline changes. It does change the speed fast. So you need to be attentive.
My 5’’ screen shows me cal, distance, time, laps...
The folding process is super easy! And like I said before it is not super heavy, and when going down to the floor is smooth, soft and slow. It does not fall fast.
It has a space where you can put your phone or tablet on the front. 2 cup (or towels or whatever) holders on the sides. And the STOP button with the strap for emergency.
Since “we” put it together I’ve been using it everyday. And I really like it. I could definitely recommended it.

Modern Guide to Golf Clubmaking Book & Golf Clubfitting Book Bundle (Buy 1, Get Second ½ Off) | Learn How to Build and Fit Golf Clubs THE MODERN GUIDE TO GOLF CLUBMAKING -BY JEFF SUMMITT-CALIFORNIA
This is a book about custom clubmaking and the craft of building a set of golf clubs from scratch. This is a very technical book that reads more like a text-book on college physics. The book takes you from how to get started to the final steps of assembly of the clubs. It covers in great detail how to set up your shop, materials inventory, to the actual manufacturing. I would not recommend this book to the person that has never built or assemble golf clubs before. This is for someone who extensive knowledge, abilities, and tools for building custom clubs and you are already in this business. A person wanting to hone their skills and learn some new techniques would find this a good reference guide. This is for the seasoned clubmaker that already possesses advanced principles and knowledge of golf club assembly.
THE MODERN GUIDE TO GOLF CLUBFITTING-BY JEFF SUMMITT-CALIFORNIA
This book along with the “MODERN GUIDE TO GOLF CLUBMAKING” come as a set and complement each other on the art and science of club fitting. It is a detailed concept book that gives the methods and parameters that works to give the custom customer their personal best with the equipment that was fitted for them. This book is based on the fact that every person is different, each swing of the club is different, the tension in the grip, and the angle of impact is unique to each individual. This book is completely structured to fit the avid golfer with the clubs that are designed and manufactured with him or her in mind. These are highly technical books and not for the enjoyment of reading but for the person who already had extensive knowledge of the sport and club building. This is a reference book with a high degree of technical information and for someone with a high degree of knowledge about this subject to begin with.
text_fidelity_b: Modern Guide to Golf Clubmaking Book & Golf Clubfitting Book Bundle (Buy 1, Get Second ½ Off) | Learn How to Build and Fit Golf Clubs

Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells: Sportneer Water Dumbbell Aerobics Workouts Set of 2 EVA Foam Pool Weights Dumbbells Set Aqua Fitness Barbells Equipment for Water Aerobics Weight Loss UPDATE: It's been a few weeks back in the water and my wife and I love these dumbbells. Seeing results. I put them through a solid workout - 3 sets of about 4-5 different movements at 15 reps. And I am HARD on them. You can get good, solid feel moving slowly, but I go fast and hard for a much heavier resistance to get my arms back up and they can take it! VERY HAPPY!

This Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells set is excellent. My wife and I love our time in the water, but one wants something more than swimming laps. And we've found the low impact of water workouts lets us do more of a workout each week, but with less strain - meaning we do other things like weights and cardio, but we also do time in the pool, giving us move overall workout time, but with lower impact. So, does that mean we also then get a solid burn? Yes.

I love power walking in the water and working my legs that way. She does more laps (ear issues keep me from joining her). So I wanted something that gave me an upper body workout. Late last year I got another set of dumbbells that are great. However, these are now (for both of us) our favorites. Why?

This Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbell set is a bit larger and gives us slightly more resistance because of it than the older pair we have. It is also slightly heavier and in turn, more resistance. We've talked about how these things look like a joke (water dumbbells), but in reality give a good, solid workout, just without the stresses that can sometimes come when you don't have the buoyancy of water. So not only great for rehab (which I used last year following surgery), but also in weekly workouts - again we feel we can get more workout time, with great results, and less stress on areas of the body giving us more overall workouts and outcomes during a week.

Taking this set into the pool, another, older couple was there (he's also recovered from past surgery, she's a PA) and asked about it. I let them try these Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells and they loved them. Said they could do things they cannot out of the water and have thought about them in the past, now think they'd get a set (though they did not ask the brand).

The set comes UNASSEMBLED, but no big deal. It's very intuitive and easy to put together. I opened it and put them together after scanning the instructions, the only part of which I caught "to make sure of," being a "pop" when you put the end pieces on. The set includes 2 extra end pieces in case you loose on. The connection is strong and tight. These are a good weight out of the water, meaning for us they are substantial and made with good materials. In the water they have a great buoyancy, so you are working to get them under the water, while they are under, and yes, you'll feel the burn. This set also has handles with straps to go around, but not lock in, the hands. I am not 100% sure it keeps them from coming off and floating away if you lost your grip - I tried and they did sort of stay in place - but I feel like I prefer the straps on these to not having them on the others. We had them out of the water, on the edge, for about 20 minutes before we left the pool and they were mostly dry. Like most areas of the country this summer, we are extremely hot and humid, so while they did not fully dry, it was enough to let them go back to where we keep them in the house - meaning they were not dripping nor made a puddle.

A set of exercises are suggested on an included sheet, which I tried to remember them while out there, but also found myself making stuff up - some of it fun and some to get the workout "look," but all of them made me work and feel it. In the end my wife and I both love these Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells and will use them often. We can use both sets together, or I think we'd both pick this set over the other when alone, just because of the increased sized and connected increased effort. Very happy with these Sportneer Water Weights Aquatic Exercise Dumbbells.

text_fidelity_a: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed I quite love this blade.. I bought the coated version to leave in my car as a utility knife, but very quickly it found its way into my pockets.. There are a few issues with this knife:  I had to immediately borrow a star key tool to change the clip over to the tang.. I don't really care if it carries tip up or down (comes tip down) but the clip is a bit large on this knife and just in the way, particularly for a knife with such great ergonomics.  The coating on the blade is also not the best.. Also mine had a few little imperfections throughout the blade- just a little pitting here and there.  Still, pretty quickly this knife has made it into my rotation.  The main reason is its ease of use.  The washers have worn in quite well and though it was a bit stiff out of the box, within a week, it opens like butter.. I've typically always favored old-school slipjoint pocket knives over locking knives for carry, but i really see the ease of one-hand use in this design.  The weight and size of the blade also really add to the inertia upon opening so it's just a really satisfying knife to flip open.. Other people might balk at the grips- I thought they felt a little cheap in the hand when I first inspected the knife, but they've turned out to be pretty solid, textured just enough to prevent slippage if they got wet.  Is it the best knife for the money?  I don't know- I bought mine for around 15 bucks and at that price wasn't expecting much:  Just a decent linerlock with a soft enough blade to easily keep sharp- something for the car-  but its size, ease of use and just good solid blade design make for a really practical tool knife which i carry more and more.
text_fidelity_b: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed

MSR Dromedary Bag Water Reservoir With a chronic migraine that hasn’t gone away in years, I’ve slept with a block of ice as the upper half of my pillow for almost as long. It’s just one of the things that really help.

Now, having a container that’ll stay ice cold all night without peeing the bed, that can be a challenge. These are the most durable water bladders I’ve found, and after a year of being frozen and thawed every day, filled to about 85-90% with a little room left for expansion, they show absolutely no real signs of wear. They’ve gotten dirty, and I’ve had to scrub them now and then, but they are very reliable. My only issue has been the tiny nozzle on the little cap, which will occasionally pop open and cause problems. That’s easily fixed with a piece of duct tape. Considering what I put these things through, I really couldn’t imagine finding a better alternative.

It would be nice if they could make the fabric covering a smoother texture, but honestly, that’s a particularly nit-picky detail that most people using these for intended purposes, couldn’t care less about.

These things last so long, if you don’t lose them and you’re not using them in active military service, I seriously doubt you’ll need to replace them for a long time to come. I bet if I’d had one while I was in the army, I’d still be using it. They’re far tougher than the 2-quart canteens I was issued, that’s for sure.
text_fidelity_b: MSR Dromedary Bag Water Reservoir

text_fidelity_a:
Merrithew at Home SPX Reformer Bundle There are several issues here to consider prior to purchasing.

1. Will the carriage roll smoothly? Even after cleaning the rails, my stott SPX failed to roll smoothly. This is a really important point.

2. Are the hand/foot loops large enough to accommodate normal sized, adult hands and feet? My stott SPX came with super tiny hand/feet loops that wouldn't work for a six year old, let alone an adult. And I have very small, adult hands.

3. Is the carriage padding sufficient? My stott SPX arrived with very thin padding and it hurt the back during movements.

4. Is this the best price on the market? Absolutely not. This package sells elsewhere on the internet for up to $500 less with additional dvd's included.

5. Will stott respond to inquiries? My phone calls and emails were ignored. It's as if this company only responds to large commercial accounts. You're completely on your own and out of luck if there is a problem or if you have a question.

6. Is the delivery box manageable? My stott SPX came in one box, approximately 14 feet long. Inside this massive box there were a couple smaller boxes. But you're talking something akin to tremendous problems getting it from curbside into the house, and if like me, you return it for being an incredible waste of money and a huge disappointment, it is painful to deal with a 14 foot box that won't fit into any normal car or suv. Hope you have a truck handy.

7. Check out other reformer brands. For a little more money the quality soars. You might think cheap is ok now, but you won't use a poor quality reformer in the long run.
text_fidelity_b: Merrithew at Home SPX Reformer Bundle

text_fidelity_a: Dart World Piranha Razor Grip 90% Tungsten Dart (24-Gram) I'm relatively newish to darts.  I've played off and on for years but still considered myself new now that I'm practicing and playing on a regular basis.  I had been playing with borrowed darts and wanted a quality set without breaking the bank and that's just what I've got in this set.  These darts feel fantastic off the fingers and they fly so much more true than my original set.  I've had fewer bounce outs with these darts.  I was skeptical of the spinning shaft.  Quite honestly the spinning portion of the shaft is made out of pretty cheap plastic but I've come to appreciate them even though I've had to replace one shaft due to a direct hit which broke the plastic.  Replacements are easily found and relatively inexpensive.  I have to agree with a previous reviewer that the spinning shaft does extend the life of the flights by spinning out when hit by another dart.  The bottom line is that you can't go wrong with these darts...they're a great bargain.  What I've learned is that while you DO want a quality dart...a higher priced dart isn't necessarily better...a quality darter thrower with a lesser set of darts will always beat a less skilled thower with a high priced set.  Find the set that suits you as a thrower...what set anyone decides to stick with is a very personal thing.
text_fidelity_b: Dart World Piranha Razor Grip 90% Tungsten Dart (24-Gram)

text_fidelity_a:
KUBEY KU085 Tactical Folding Knife G10 Handle Stainless Steel Blade Bearing Flipper Hunting Pocket Camping Survival Outdoor Knife (#KU087) Nice knife, especially at this price point. BUT, there are some issues. To me it appeared that this this knife is inferred as being spring assisted. It is most definitely not spring assisted as all other knives are determined to be. The thumb hole is difficult for me to use in one smooth motion. I thought that surely the flipper would be spring assisted, but no. It takes it to half open and no more. You need to use a wrist flip or two hands to finish the opening. That would not be much of a problem, but that makes it illegal to carry here in central Ohio. Sad.

One last thing. This blade is nowhere near 4 inches. It is measured at 3.5 inches. How does Kubey justify these irregularities? Perhaps this is just something being lost in translation.

This knife is super sharp. Locks up like a vault. No wobbles anywhere. It handles well. And it is beautiful. It is definitely worth the money as long as you know up front what you are buying. The build quality is there. The cosmetics are there. It doesn't need this type of advertising to sell. Thus the four stars. I would buy again and I will probably buy from Kubey again.

The screws holding the clip have become loose. I am in the process of buying a torx bit set so I can tighten them. I wish that this clip could be switched for tip up carry, but the clip orientation cannot be changed.

Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ This is the best thermos I've owned to date, but it's far from perfect.

If you put piping hot coffee in it, it will keep it hot for about 45 minutes, and keep it warm for about 2 more hours after that. I haven't used it for cold drinks.

I love the handle style; that's my favorite part about it. Most handled thermoses have this infuriating issue of the mouthpiece never lining up properly with where the handle is, so you always have to hold them weirdly to drink from them. On this thermos, the handle is fabric, and can be adjusted 360 degrees around the thermos, so no matter where the mouthpiece ends up, you can just adjust the handle to be right where you need it. the other nice thing about the fabric handle is that you won't break it by bumping it into things or dropping it.

The worst part about this thing is cleaning it. The entire head of it is very complex, with lots of moving parts, springs, and plastic bits - ALL of which are submerged in whatever you are drinking. So, when you take the lid off, you have disassemble the whole thing and either soak all the parts, or wash them all individually. Don't be lazy and put off cleaning it until the next day or you'll have whatever you drank caked all though the innards. If you don't mind keeping it clean, it's really nice. I'm very happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ

Since adjustment is really only necessary during initial setup I sometimes put a drop of super-glue on to prevent it from moving over time as I clean my glasses. But I spend at least a couple weeks using them before making the set-up permanent.

The original had foam based tape. Theoretically this gave it better surface area adhesion on typically curved glasses. The thin base of this product is a little flexible and seems to conform to the glass so I appear to get similar adhesion. Those who complained about bad adhesive probably touched the tape or tried to mount onto unclean glass/plastic. The tape I got was good quality. You should use a pin and tweezers to handle the tape. Also, make sure you don't touch/contaminate the mount face and insure your glasses are very clean.

The reflective surface, so far, seems at least the same as the original product. I must guess a bit because my ViewPoint's are 10 years old and a comparison may not be fair. This product could be worse but the original has degraded over time.

There are definitely several ways this COULD be inferior but so far they appear equal. Only time will tell more.

I found a package that I believe was purchased in 2002 with a price of $10.99 on it so, comparatively, the price isn't completely horrible although it is still high.

Note: For road bike use, mount it as high as comfortable on your glasses so you don't end up looking at your shoulder when on your bike. Also, be sure to have your helmet on to insure it's not in the way of your view.
text_fidelity_b: Third Eye On-Lens Micro Bicycle Mirror

text_fidelity_a:
UUQ C4-12X50 Rifle Scope Dual Illuminated Reticle W/Laser Sight and Holographic Red Dot Reflex Sight Everyone knows the first rule: You get what you pay for. In this case though I think that you get more than what you expect. My experience so far is that this scope functions flawlessly. That has proven how well the Chinese can reverse engineer some products and manufacture them to relatively high standards. I would certainly be afraid to drop it but it is screwed together very well.

The second rule I abide by is: The more complicated the product, the more things that can go wrong with it. And this particular product has a lot of technical features. Think of it as a Swiss Army Knife but with battery powered components. It is actually designed quite well and looks good properly mounted but I doubt that it would continuously handle the recoil from a large caliber rifle or shotgun. However there is a 30 day "Money Back Satisfaction Guarantee" and a 12-month warranty if it goes bad.

The third rule that I usually follow is to buy at least one model higher (in price and quality) when I determine what I might need. In this case though it makes more sense to not get a more complicated scope/laser combo. Shooting/hunting is complicated enough depending on how your weapon functions, the conditions you're shooting under, and your ability to master the situation to end up successful. Typically the more things that can get in your way during a shooting situation can limit your results dramatically. So I always try to keep it simple.

This is a fun product however -- just make sure that you use it a lot during the initial 12 months. By then you will know what functions are most important to you, which weapon pairs with it the best (for you), and how dependable it is. Perhaps you only need a fixed blade knife instead of that Swiss Army Knife.
text_fidelity_b: UUQ C4-12X50 Rifle Scope Dual Illuminated Reticle W/Laser Sight and Holographic Red Dot Reflex Sight

text_fidelity_a:
Vmotal Night Vision and Day Binoculars - Digital Infrared with Night Vision in 100% Darkness with 2.5" LCD Screen, 1080P Full HD, True IR Illuminator for Hunting & Surveillance Unboxing the night vision goggle/camera had everything in its place and ready to set up. Setting up is pretty simple. Four batteries go on each side of the goggles and the covers lock tight afterwards. A few things include the goggle outer case design as it is easy to hold and the case is easy to grip. They also included a decent quality padded and adjustable strap for more safety. The goggles have metal clips that hold the strap on each side making it a strong design. The goggles weigh 1.94 pounds with batteries. The carrying case is above average in quality with a carrying handle. The goggles fit secure in one direction and have a separate section for the cables, cleaning cloth, strap, user manual and room for more of your own items.

There are the 6 user buttons 3 on each side and are placed in a good position for feel to the fingers and they are easy to remember what each button does. There are an average amount of settings under the menu button. Mainly photo and video quality that you can choose plus some other sensitivity settings such as brightness and IR settings along with date and time and storage settings. One added feature in the menu is a Burst setting (on/off) and it is for fast acting shots. Note: The higher the camera resolution is set, the longer it takes the media to process, just something to keep in mind.

On shutdown the goggles remember all your custom settings. The goggles can handle up to a 32GB micro SD card. Don't worry that is 9999 pictures in HQ and 2.37 min in HD video. I didn't notice any difference in quality with FHD setting and storage time. If you connect the included USB cable to your computer and goggles and set the goggles in play mode, viewing media is a lot better quality than in the goggles view finder. In the photos I uploaded, I show a picture in the woods set at 1M pixels 1280X960. Notice a bit grainy on an overcast day. On testing the highest setting at 3M pixels 2048X1200 was about the same on overcast day. There is another picture of white flowers in full sun at the highest resolution setting. Last, there is an indoor picture of piano keys close up at the highest resolution setting.

Here is something that is not in the goggles manual: You can use your camera and photo computer software (Windows 10) for capturing video and photos from your goggles live using the goggles USB port. Make sure the goggles are in Mode/PC Cam and your computer camera software window is open. Another feature is you can copy the media to your computer using this mode. The goggles in Mode/ MSDC mode is for loading your goggles micro SD card media to your computer. Simultaneously you can use the goggles mode button to switch between both while plugged into the USB port.

Final Thoughts: This item in my opinion is for IR use at night time. The video and photo quality are crisp and clear for that purpose and the goggles give 7 IR settings for brightness, a good feature when viewing in dark and distant places. I wouldn't use the goggles for making family media because the goggles have
a bit of grain under certain lighting and color conditions but not in IR modes. The goggles do very well in IR modes. I did my test using rechargeable lithium 1.5 volt batteries because they do hold a steady voltage longer than alkalines. To sum it all up, I personally feel this item is a good choice for the cost.
text_fidelity_b: Vmotal Night Vision and Day Binoculars - Digital Infrared with Night Vision in 100% Darkness with 2.5" LCD Screen, 1080P Full HD, True IR Illuminator for Hunting & Surveillance

Bonnlo Boat Kayak Canoe Cart Carrier Dolly Trailer Tote Trolley Transport Kayak Accessories Large with 20x2mm Aluminum Pipe Double Kickstands, Inflation Free Solid Tire Wheels, 2 Ratchet Straps This was pretty easy to assemble, it appears very well made. Good wheels, straps and metal.

No matter how tight I make the two bands to the boat, they slide about a bit.

The wheels will tip to the right or left depending on how much the restraining bands shift.

I am using this trolley with an Old Town Pack Canoe. Those are bit shorter and wider in middle then many canoes. Thus it is easy for the bands to shift about, especially if you plan to pull the canoe with the wheels on the back end of the canoe. Were the move over pavement or other very smooth ground, it may go well. I have to move my canoe from back of yard over uneven ground and that causes the straps to shift on one side or the other.

When strap on on side slides back, the wheels won't run true and the canoe will be pulling in that direction. This will continue until you can't pull the canoe at all and have to reset the whole thing. For a long portage, this won't work.

The second time I used this thing, I put the trolley on the front and pushed it and things went better over a short distance. It was still balking and it was not a smooth run.

Next time I use it, I will try to set the trolley in the center of canoe and see how that goes. I expect some more experimentation will result in usable solution. But, if you have a fatter canoe with more of a narrowing at front and back, have to transport over uneven ground, and want to pull the canoe instead of pushing it; there may be things may not go well.
text_fidelity_b: Bonnlo Boat Kayak Canoe Cart Carrier Dolly Trailer Tote Trolley Transport Kayak Accessories Large with 20x2mm Aluminum Pipe Double Kickstands, Inflation Free Solid Tire Wheels, 2 Ratchet Straps

text_fidelity_a:
Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel i have bought some really expensive beds over the past few years and i have done much research to get a good bed. i have not succeeded. so i decided to go with this. TPU does not stretch as many commented on and so it stays inflated. i put a foam 2" topper on top of this and it's like a regular bed, but i think it is better. yes the inflator pump sucks but it does the job. i am not going back to a normal bed. just have to dial in the air pressure now for the ideal feel. i wish i had not spent all that money on the last bed. worth noting that the size can be an issue when fitting sheets. it's in between double and queen size. consider jersey sheets in double since they stretch.

update
ok so the negative vote i got made me think and i realize most of the review is about how regular beds suck and not how this bed is awesome, so time for an update. one of the great features i already mentioned, no stretching or leaks so the bed stays firm. another good feature is the connections inside the bed. the system they use allows for a fairly flat surface because the seal points are not form top to bottom but have a linkage that allows the bed to inflate to a fairly consistent depth across the surface. the image shows it well. other air beds have deep pockets where the weld connects the top to bottom piece. that is a major deal if you have ever slept on an airbed like this. flat surface is key. this bed seems to have the most advanced welding. the only real issue i have is that the bed is so light weight that it moves around easily on the frame. that can be annoying. Costco sells this same item and i sell to Costco so i know how intensely they review items for consideration to sell. this is the best airbed on the market today, period.

text_fidelity_a: Klean Kanteen TKWide 16oz (w/Café Cap) - Tofu I quite like this bottle.  I bought this in the 16 oz size and i maybe should have gone larger, as i really like the design.  I use this one for coffee, though If it were larger i would keep water in it.  The thing I like about this over others in the Kleen Kanteen range is the lip and threading.  The classic bottles have threading on the outside of the lip of the bottle with a cap which screws over the lip, clamping its edge against a gasket.  I have come to find this design prone to leaks if the gasket isn't properly seated.  The TKWide range just doesn't have this problem.  The threading is on the inside, low, under the lip of the bottle and the cap screws into it with a simple o ring.  I'm not a huge fan of the "cafe cap" but i just remove it and drink from the lip of the bottle which is itself quite comfortable.  It's kleer that kleen kanteen designed this bottle to work in exactly this way, as the lip of the bottle is the most comfortable of any i've ever encountered to drink from and they even make an assortment of different caps for this line with different features.  I'm considering getting the simple steel loop or bamboo cap to eliminate all remaining unnecessary parts.  The user experience drinking from the bottle with cap removed is similar to drinking from a tall glass tumbler.  The threading is recessed from the lip and doesn't interfere with drinking at all.. I also like that the 'cafe cap' is easily disassembled.. I hate cleaning these things, once a few weeks of coffee residue gets on them.  I've dropped this bottle twice and it has a dent now, but nothing severe.  I find it well made and well engineered and though, in my head at least, this bottle rivals the yeti ramblers which are similar, its about half of the price or less.

text_fidelity_a:
Isokinetics Inc. Adjustable Back Exercise Ball Office Chair - Standard or (Exclusive)"Tall Boy" Frame Height - with 52cm Ball - Office size 60mm/2.5" wheels - w/Starter Pump and Ball Measuring Tape Very well designed chair. Very excellent value for people with back problems. At this price point you have to take a flyer with this chair if you have back issues!

My specific back issues allow me to sit in the chair for only a few hours. I let my chiropractor borrow the chair for a few days. Folks in the office either liked it or didn't.

I'm 6 feet. I definitely needed the accessory leg lift kit.

Two small issues:
1) The nuts that keep the metal retainer bar in place dig into fairly soft plastic and the torquing of the chair in use works the nuts loose. I'm always finding a nut on the floor and I have to re-tighten. Need to add a lock washer and firm up the plastic the nut interfaces to.

2) Two wheels come with locking mechanisms. No matter where you put these wheels you end up locking the wheels somehow. A couple Amazon reviewers recommend using the two back wheels, but I still lock one or the other. If you use the back wheels, then if you don't remember to check for locked when you sit down, then when you get up you will knock the chair over backwards since the chair is so light.

I found a workaround to #2. I Took pliers and twisted off the tab that controls the locking mechanism, then used a knife to shave off the locking lever plastic, to make sure shoes, etc. don't snag and lock the wheels. The locking mechanism still works fine, but now I have to use my fingernail to flip the lever. Problem solved!

I would definitely recommend you try this chair!
text_fidelity_b: Isokinetics Inc. Adjustable Back Exercise Ball Office Chair - Standard or (Exclusive)"Tall Boy" Frame Height - with 52cm Ball - Office size 60mm/2.5" wheels - w/Starter Pump and Ball Measuring Tape

text_fidelity_a: RaceWax Ski P-tex Base Repair Kit: 10 ptex, Metal Scraper, 3 3M Buffing Pads Got this to do some repair work on my 30 something year old xc skis.  Worked great and so easy to do.  I had some pretty bad gouges and scraps from skiing on frozen gravel.  Spent a bit of time preping the bases by removing the wax base and cleaning up the edges of the gouges.  I also used my waxing iron to preheat the bases.  Lit the candle and moved slowly and carefully.  Keep the candle close to your work and hold it at an angle to keep the carbon to a minimum.  After cooling down the included scraper mad quick work of leveling out the area.  A couple quick passes with the scotch brite pads and a finally buff with the white pad and I was ready for a base wax.  I have only been out once since the repair (figures all the snow melted) but the repair held perfectly.  I used about a third of a candle to repair about 4 ft. of scratches of at least a fingernail width wide.  So much cheaper than a new pair of skis.
text_fidelity_b: RaceWax Ski P-tex Base Repair Kit: 10 ptex, Metal Scraper, 3 3M Buffing Pads

text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack Commercial Studio Cycle Surprised myself by investing in this bike. I've never purchased any major exercise equipment before, but I did take a spin class years ago that just completely kicked my butt. I always felt interested in trying it again, but I am the not the type who enjoys going to gyms or attending classes in person. So the iFit setup and such intrigued me enough to give it a try.

Firstly, don't believe Amazon when they allow you to schedule a date of delivery. I scheduled my bike to be delivered weeeeeeks in advance. The delivery date was missed with no call or update. It was also impossible to reach a customer service rep. Thankfully my husband works from home, so I wasn't taking time off of work to wait around for no reason.

When the bike did arrive, it was easy to unbox and assemble, though I did have help from my husband. One issue we encountered was the seat was misthreaded into the holder. This was bad as when I went to adjust it, you couldnt turn it to loosen or tighten it. The seat was all half on there, and unfortunately not coming out. Thankfully my husband is super handy as he had to drill it out, rethread the setup and got it installed. Whew!

I have now had the bike for a good few months with no other issues. It's quiet, takes up a small footprint, and quite a challenge for a weakling like myself.

Now, if this bike didn't have the iFit programs, I likely wouldn't use it. Those programs make the bike work for me. I love the selection (though I wish there were more beginner programs). I still need to do more of the off-bike workouts as well.....and I haven't tried the live classes yet. But the fact that I have so many options that keep changing makes me come back. I also love the series styled workouts. :)

All in all I am way happy with this bike. I can see myself using this for years to come, and I will gladly continue my iFit subscription after my trial is over.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack Commercial Studio Cycle

text_fidelity_a:
Energizer LED Camping Lantern, 240-400 High Lumens, IPX4 Water Resistant, Battery Powered LED, Use For Camping, Hiking, Emergency Light, Batteries Included I got this LED lantern to use as an emergency light and for when we need an area flashlight at night on our farm. It's worked well for this purpose. I no longer camp, but my first thought on testing this lantern was that I wished I'd had something like this back in my camping days. It's very bright compared to other lantern flashlights I've had in the past, but you can dim the light to about half strength using the dimmer button. You can use the lantern as a directional light or extend the light up above the base to make it an area light. There's a stand that can be pulled out from the back of the base so you can put the lantern on a table or floor. The orange grip is lightly textured and rubber-like for a secure hold when carrying it.

When you rotate the light upward, the white plastic back reflector is exposed. This is how you access the battery area. There are two flat-screw-head type locks that need to be rotated clockwise by a quarter turn to access the batteries. I actually opened them using the back of a clothespin. lol. The lantern comes with 4 batteries, but it can take 8 AA batteries--for longer life, I assume, but I've not tried it.

The on-off button is on the back of the base. You push the button to turn the light on or off, or you hold it to dim the light and release the button when the light is at the desired level. At first, I occasionally had trouble with not removing my finger quickly enough from the button and getting a dim instead of turning the light off. I just needed to learn to "jab" the button rather than taking my time. The lantern looks fairly durable and easy to clean, but I've only given it light use so far.

The instruction manual is pretty brief, but it does cover all the "how to use" information. Instructions you might wish to know now: "To disable Try Me mode, remove batteries from compartment and wait 10 seconds. Reinsert batteries and wait 10 seconds before pressing switch." and "Lantern is water resistant and suitable for use outside. Do not submerse or attempt to operate under water."

According to the packaging, the light was made in China and the batteries were made in Singapore.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer LED Camping Lantern, 240-400 High Lumens, IPX4 Water Resistant, Battery Powered LED, Use For Camping, Hiking, Emergency Light, Batteries Included

text_fidelity_a:
WATERH Smart Water Bottle - Tracks Hydration Intake, Analyzes TDS Water Quality, LED Glow Reminder via Bluetooth. Hack Your Hydration Health, 18 oz The WATERH bottle looks and feels solid. It's comfortable to grab for a person with large hands like me, but I wonder how a person with smaller hands would feel about it. I have certainly used other "non-smart" bottles that feel better in my hands. The cap is functional, though I would have preferred a type of cap that has a spout or similar mechanism. For example, I love the Zojirushi cap that (1) keeps any parts where you place your lips clean (WATERH does that), (2) can be operated with one hand (WATERH does NOT do that; you need a hand to hold the bottle and the second one to open the cap), and (3) is easy to clean (the WATERH cap has some tight spaces that are hard to clean).

The bottle has a water sensor inside, as well as some kind of scales at the bottom of the bottle that helps the app determine how much water you have consumed. The bottle needs to be charged by resting it on a USB-C base charger, included with the product. I've been using the water bottle for a couple of days, and the bottle battery is at 97%, so apparently it will last quite long.

The bottle has a led ring near the base that reminds you when to drink. The led light is also used to display when the bottle is charging, when it is fully charged, etc.

The application is pretty basic and bare bones. The Apple Store display pretty bad customer reviews. I haven't found it to be bad. The only missing feature that is important to me is an automatic connection with Apple's Health application. Adding that feature would make much more useful to me.

The manufacturer states that "WaterH is equipped with a built-in TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) sensor meter so you can know exactly what's in your bottle. Stop guessing the quality of your water through taste or smell." The sensor is likely there, but I have found not way to access those results. There are no instructions, and exploring the app yielded nothing.

Bottomline: the WATERH water bottle is a fun gimmick, but not really necessary. Regardless of how you do it, drink plenty of water.
text_fidelity_b: WATERH Smart Water Bottle - Tracks Hydration Intake, Analyzes TDS Water Quality, LED Glow Reminder via Bluetooth. Hack Your Hydration Health, 18 oz

Cola Bottle Vacuum Insulated Double Wall Stainless Steel Leak-proof Cola Shape Sports Water Bottle Keeps Your Drink Hot & Cold 17oz(500ml) The Skyline 17 oz premium insulated stainless steel bottle is a great choice! I own several S'Well bottles that look and function identical to this one at a MUCH lower price. A co-worker really liked my S'Well bottle but as previously stated, S'Well bottles are $25+ a bottle and that's more than I wanted to spend on a gift, so I was looking for a comparable alternative and I found it with the FLY Skyline. I wanted to make sure the Fly Skyline would keep water ice cold all day, I filled the Skyline bottle with ice cold water the before work and the bottle was effective at keeping the water ice cold the next day. The bottle is constructed of high quality stainless steel and looks/feels like it will last forever. The bottle holds 17 ounces of liquid, which is perfect for taking to work to be able to drink ice cold water at your desk. The lip on the bottle provides a very comfortable surface to drink from. The bottle includes a screw on lid that provides a leak-proof seal eliminating the worry and fear that the liquid will spill out of the bottle. The bottle states that it can keep beverages hot for 12 hours and cold for 24; I have only used the bottle for keeping beverages cold so I can only confirm that it can keep beverages cold for 24 hours (not sure about effectiveness of ability to keep beverages hot as I have not tried). The opening will easily accommodate "half moon" shaped ice but you will struggle to place ice cubes in the opening. Overall I was very satisfied with this bottle so if you are looking for a bottle that will keep your beverage hot/cold all day the Skyline stainless steel coke bottle is a great choice!

Pros:
-Keeps water cold/hot for a long time
-Stainless steel construction will last forever
-Screw top provides leak-proof seal
-Great textured surface makes holding onto bottle easy and slip free

I was fortunate enough to have received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased opinion. I would definitely purchase this bottle again.
